data.name: v1.40.2
data.body:
**Summary of changes**:

* Upstream security fixes:
  - [eMudhra intermediate CA compromise](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/):
    release: updated the `distroless` docker image base to pick up the patched
    `ca-certificates` package (`20250419+deb13u1`), so it no longer trusts the roots of the
    compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs. The distroless image released in 1.40.1 still
    shipped the unpatched bundle.

**Docker images**:
    https://hub.docker.com/r/envoyproxy/envoy/tags?page=1&name=v1.40.2
**Docs**:
    https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.40.2/
**Release notes**:
    https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/v1.40.2/version_history/v1.40/v1.40.2
**Full changelog**:
    https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/compare/v1.40.1...v1.40.2

Signed-off-by: Jonh Wendell <jwendell@redhat.com>

data.name: v1.21.1
data.body:
# Improvements
Rook v1.21.1 is a patch release limited in scope and focusing on feature additions and bug fixes to the Ceph operator.

- security: Enforce secure msgr2 mode for mon connections (#18324, @pujitha24)
- cluster: Allow configuring the Prometheus scrape timeout (#18424, @harshilv17)
- clusterdisruption: Fix minimum failure domain detection for region (#18577, @NUAAwqy)
- object: Add CephObjectStoreUser secretTemplate (#18469, @jhoblitt)
- core: Disable insecure global id reclaim instead of muting the warning (#18597, @travisn)
- mgr: Compare prometheus scrape interval numerically to avoid unnecessary updates (#18583, @cvas22)
- nvmeof: Enable SPDK interrupt mode to reduce idle CPU usage (#18599, @OdedViner)
- nvmeof: Preserve gateway Service across scale-down to keep stable ClusterIP (#18584, @OdedViner)
- nvmeof: Add external client access documentation (#17719, @OdedViner)
- docs: Delete storageclass before helm upgrade to v1.21 (#18574, @travisn)
- object: Emit rgwCommandFlags in a deterministic order to avoid unnecessary restarts (#18592, @travisn)
- core: Add status message on custom resources (#18533, @AnikaYadav1)
- object: Ignore the dashboard's per-realm credential map (#18425, @UmanShahzad)
- osd: Avoid empty label selector when all OSDs in batch are skipped (#18564, @trukhinyuri)
- object: add trafficDistribution to the RGW service spec (#18541, @bo0tzz)
- osd: Skip nbd, drbd, and zram devices in device discovery (#18490, @jhoblitt)
- osd: Reject purely numeric topology values in validation (#18539, @OdedViner)
- nfs: Clean up temporary ganesha config files (#18538, @kediyalua)
- ci: Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 to fix govulncheck (#18540, @OdedViner)
- ci: Build release images with the newest Go patch release (#18609, @jhoblitt)

data.name: Release v2.15.2
data.body:
## Changelog

Refer to the [2.15 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.14.x.

### Go Version

- 1.27.3, which contains mitigations for CVE-2026-111943 by distrusting eMudhra intermediate certificates (#8798)

### Dependencies

- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.20.3 (#8798)
- golang.org/x/crypto v0.58.0 (#8798)
- golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0 (#8798)

### Fixed

General

- Allowed connection types are now correctly respected in auth callout setups
- Fixed a potential queue sub weight amplification in the sublist
- OCSP responses are now correctly bound to the certificate serial number

JetStream

- Restored v1 stream snapshots now correctly guard against excessive subject lengths, subject counts or block counts

Leafnodes

- ACLs on leafnode connections no longer override allow/deny lists to implicitly allow `$MQTT.>` permissions

MQTT

- OCSP verification for MQTT connections now correctly obeys the `ocsp_peer` option in the `mqtt` block

### Complete Changes

https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/compare/v2.15.1...v2.15.2

This is release 1.85.0 ([googol](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/g_stands_for.md)) of gRPC Core.

For gRPC documentation, see [grpc.io](https://grpc.io/). For previous releases, see [Releases](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/releases).

This release contains refinements, improvements, and bug fixes, with highlights listed below.


Core
---

-  [Backport][v1.85.x][security] Update gRPC repo roots. ([#43717](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43717))
-  [experiments] Add map_host_header_to_authority experiment. ([#43561](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43561))
-  [Security] Add MLKEM1024 as a key exchange option. ([#43514](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43514))
-  Remove OpenSSL1.0.2 Support. ([#43466](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43466))
-  [Autosharding-LB][Part-1] Implementing A119. ([#43406](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43406))
-  [OpenSSL] Add support for OpenSSL 4. ([#41932](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/41932))
-  [A110] Add child channel options. ([#43314](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43314))

C#
---

-  [Build] Disambiguate protobuf_version in templates. ([#43433](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43433))

Python
---

-  [Python][AIO] Fixed data race in PollerCompletionQueue. ([#43429](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43429))
-  [Python] Fix SyncServicerContext abort not raising exception. ([#43126](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43126))
-  [Python] Fixed channelz module leak. ([#43196](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43196))
-  [Python] Fixed CSDS memory leak. ([#43202](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43202))
-  [Python] Unpin Cython dependency for source builds. ([#43378](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/pull/43378))

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Fluentd no longer depends on yajl-ruby, because yajl-ruby cannot be built on Ruby 4.1.
>
> * Plugin authors: if your plugin uses `require 'yajl'`, please migrate to the json gem. If you keep using yajl-ruby, declare it in your gemspec.
> * Users: if you see `LoadError: cannot load such file -- yajl`, add yajl-ruby to your Gemfile. This works only on Ruby 4.0 or earlier.

### Bug Fix

* https://github.com/fluent/fluentd/pull/5574 gem: remove yajl-ruby from runtime dependencies for Ruby 4.1
  * Plugins that `require 'yajl'` need to declare yajl-ruby in their own gemspec.
  * If you see `LoadError: cannot load such file -- yajl`, add yajl-ruby to your Gemfile. This works only on Ruby 4.0 or earlier.

### Contributors to this release (Alphabetical order)

* Shizuo Fujita

data.name: v1.155.0
data.body:
## [v1.155.0](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/releases/tag/v1.155.0)

Released at 2026-10-23

**Update Note 1:** `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): `/admin/tenants` requests without `start` and `end` query args now return tenants for the current day. This is a breaking change because previously it was expected to return all tenants. If you still need to retrieve all tenants, set the `start` and `end` params so that the resulting time range fully includes the `-retentionPeriod`. Also note that [vmctl](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmctl/victoriametrics/) is known to send requests to `/admin/tenants` under the hood when migrating data between VictoriaMetrics deployments. Therefore, make sure that you run `vmctl` with both `*-filter-time-start` and `*-filter-time-end` params. See the updated [URL format](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/#url-format) and [#11791](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11791) for details.

* SECURITY: upgrade Go builder from Go1.27.2 to Go1.27.3. See [the list of issues addressed in Go1.27.3](https://github.com/golang/go/issues?q=milestone%3AGo1.27.3%20label%3ACherryPickApproved).
* SECURITY: upgrade base docker image (Alpine) from 3.24.2 to 3.24.3. See [Alpine 3.24.4 release notes](https://alpinelinux.org/posts/Alpine-3.21.9-3.22.7-3.23.7-3.24.3-released.html).

* FEATURE: all VictoriaMetrics components: add `-healthcheck` command-line flag, which checks that the running process accepts connections at `-httpListenAddr` and exits with non-zero code if the check fails. This allows setting up Docker `HEALTHCHECK` in images without `curl` or `wget`. See [these docs](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/url-examples/#health) and [VictoriaLogs#1565](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaLogs/issues/1565).
* FEATURE: all VictoriaMetrics components: expose `process_cpu_cores_host`, `process_cpu_cores_cgroup_quota`, `process_memory_host_bytes` and `process_memory_cgroup_bytes` metrics. Cgroup metrics are `-1` if no cgroup limit is set or the limit cannot be read. See [#11460](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11460).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): deprecate Server URL editing and show a warning when using a saved custom URL. Existing custom URLs continue to work. See [#11735](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11735).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): update the appearance of error, warning, info, and success messages. See [#11736](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11736).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): add a tenant column to Top Queries and Active Queries when tenant information is available. See [#6346](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/6346).
* FEATURE: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): limit tenant discovery to the selected time range. See [#11784](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11784).
* FEATURE: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/) and [Single-node VictoriaMetrics](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/): limit the number of logged parse errors per each scrape of a target via `-promscrape.maxParseErrorsPerScrape` command-line flag (20 by default). The number of suppressed parse errors is logged after the scrape. This prevents log flooding from targets exposing many malformed lines. See [#8856](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/8856).
* FEATURE: [vmalert](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmalert/): restore Prometheus compatibility for alerts state restoration, so Prometheus can be used as `-remoteRead.url` again. Previously, the restore query used MetricsQL function `default_rollup()` which Prometheus rejects, so the state of alerting rules with `for > 0` was reset on every vmalert restart. See [#11574](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11574).
* FEATURE: `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): export `vm_request_duration_seconds{path="/admin/tenants"}` for tracking time it takes to fetch [tenants](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/#multitenancy) from the database.
* FEATURE: [dashboards](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/tree/master/dashboards): apply the instance filter to the `CPU pressure`, `Memory pressure`, `IO pressure`, and `Memory allocations rate` panels in the Resource usage section of the [VictoriaMetrics - cluster](https://grafana.com/grafana/dashboards/11176-victoriametrics-cluster/) dashboard. Displays zero disk I/O and syscall rates. See [#11742](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11742).
* FEATURE: [alerts-health](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/blob/master/deployment/docker/rules/alerts-health.yml): add `TooManySnapshots` alerting rule. It notifies about instances where more than 2 [snapshots](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#how-to-work-with-snapshots) are stored for at least 2 hours. Such snapshots are usually left behind by failed `vmbackup` / `vmbackupmanager` runs. They keep references to the already merged data parts and prevent [background merges](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#storage) from freeing the disk space, which results in excessive disk usage. See [#9344](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/9344).

* BUGFIX: [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/): prevent [Kafka remote write](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/integrations/kafka/) getting stuck after TLS certificates are reloaded. Previously, when vmagent detected changed certificates and restarted the Kafka producer, pending sends to the old producer could hang forever and the remote write queue stopped draining until vmagent was restarted. Now such sends are retried with the new producer. See [#11737](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11737).
* BUGFIX: `vminsert` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): prevent metric metadata drops after transient RPC handshake timeouts when connecting to `vmstorage`. See [#11762](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11762). Thanks to @sakateka for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/), [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/) and `vminsert` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): properly validate time series ingested via [`/api/v1/import/native`](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#how-to-import-data-in-native-format). See [#11745](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11745). Thanks to @meshchellomishel for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/): reduce memory usage during for Kubernetes service discovery, when scrape configuration has many entries that matches small subset of targets. See [#11751](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/pull/11751). Thanks to @CamberLoid for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and `vmstorage` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): prevent search requests panic. See [#11788](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11788) for details.
* BUGFIX: [vmsingle](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/) and [vmagent](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmagent/): set `__meta_kubernetes_namespace` and the namespace metadata to the namespace of the `Endpoints` or `EndpointSlice` object in [`role: endpoints`](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/sd_configs/#kubernetes_sd_configs) and `role: endpointslice` service discovery when the referenced pod lives in another namespace. Previously the namespace of the pod was used, unlike Prometheus. See [#11798](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11798). Thanks to @cestercian for contribution.
* BUGFIX: [vmauth](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/): skip keys with unsupported `kty` or `crv`, missing required members or invalid values in the JWKS fetched via [OIDC discovery](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/vmauth/#oidc-discovery) instead of rejecting the whole key set, as required by [RFC 7517](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7517#section-5). Previously, a single unsupported or malformed key in the JWKS caused vmauth to reject all JWTs from that issuer, including tokens signed with supported keys. See [#11748](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11748).
* BUGFIX: [vmui](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/single-server-victoriametrics/#vmui): stop saving the automatically calculated query step in shared URLs, so opening a link recalculates the step for the selected time range and screen width. Explicitly configured steps remain fixed. See [#11638](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11638).
* BUGFIX: `vmselect` in [VictoriaMetrics cluster](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/): change the default time range for [/admin/tenants](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/#multitenancy) HTTP endpoint to search tenants only for the current day instead of searching the entire `[0, now]` time range. This should prevent unnecessary load on `vmstorage` and prevent OOMs. See the updated [URL format](https://docs.victoriametrics.com/victoriametrics/cluster-victoriametrics/#url-format) and [#11791](https://github.com/VictoriaMetrics/VictoriaMetrics/issues/11791) for details.

Bump version to 19.4.48 by Chef Expeditor

Obvious fix; these changes are the result of automation not creative thinking.

## Installation one-liner

```shell
kubectl apply -f https://infra.tekton.dev/tekton-releases/pipeline/previous/v1.17.1/release.yaml
```

## Attestation

The Rekor UUID for this release is `108e9186e8c5677ac8e702d8f174d6509e26698a2f0c98fe78c04629b3a92414e2e9ae50696b433c`

Obtain the attestation:
```shell
REKOR_UUID=108e9186e8c5677ac8e702d8f174d6509e26698a2f0c98fe78c04629b3a92414e2e9ae50696b433c
rekor-cli get --uuid $REKOR_UUID --format json | jq -r .Attestation | jq .
```

Verify that all container images in the attestation are in the release file:
```shell
RELEASE_FILE=https://infra.tekton.dev/tekton-releases/pipeline/previous/v1.17.1/release.yaml
REKOR_UUID=108e9186e8c5677ac8e702d8f174d6509e26698a2f0c98fe78c04629b3a92414e2e9ae50696b433c

# Obtains the list of images with sha from the attestation
REKOR_ATTESTATION_IMAGES=$(rekor-cli get --uuid "$REKOR_UUID" --format json | jq -r .Attestation | jq -r '.subject[]|.name + ":v1.17.1@sha256:" + .digest.sha256')

# Download the release file
curl -L "$RELEASE_FILE" > release.yaml

# For each image in the attestation, match it to the release file
for image in $REKOR_ATTESTATION_IMAGES; do
  printf $image; grep -q $image release.yaml && echo " ===> ok" || echo " ===> no match";
done
```

data.name: v3.7.3
data.body:
Please check out [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/CHANGELOG/CHANGELOG-3.7.md) for a full list of changes. And make sure to read [upgrade guide](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.7/upgrades/upgrade_3_7/) before upgrading etcd (there may be breaking changes).

For installation guides, please check out [play.etcd.io](http://play.etcd.io) and [operating etcd](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.7/op-guide/). Latest support status for common architectures and operating systems can be found at [supported platforms](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.7/op-guide/supported-platform/).

###### Linux

```sh
ETCD_VER=v3.7.3

# choose either URL
GOOGLE_URL=https://storage.googleapis.com/etcd
GITHUB_URL=https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/download
DOWNLOAD_URL=${GOOGLE_URL}

rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz
rm -rf /tmp/etcd-download-test && mkdir -p /tmp/etcd-download-test

curl -L ${DOWNLOAD_URL}/${ETCD_VER}/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz -o /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz
tar xzvf /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz -C /tmp/etcd-download-test --strip-components=1 --no-same-owner
rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-linux-amd64.tar.gz

/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcd --version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdutl version

# start a local etcd server
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcd

# write,read to etcd
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl --endpoints=localhost:2379 put foo bar
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl --endpoints=localhost:2379 get foo
```

###### macOS (Darwin)

```sh
ETCD_VER=v3.7.3

# choose either URL
GOOGLE_URL=https://storage.googleapis.com/etcd
GITHUB_URL=https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/releases/download
DOWNLOAD_URL=${GOOGLE_URL}

rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip
rm -rf /tmp/etcd-download-test && mkdir -p /tmp/etcd-download-test

curl -L ${DOWNLOAD_URL}/${ETCD_VER}/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip -o /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip
unzip /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip -d /tmp && rm -f /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64.zip
mv /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64/* /tmp/etcd-download-test && rm -rf mv /tmp/etcd-${ETCD_VER}-darwin-amd64

/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcd --version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdctl version
/tmp/etcd-download-test/etcdutl version
```

###### Docker

etcd uses [`gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd`](https://gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd) as a primary container registry, and [`quay.io/coreos/etcd`](https://quay.io/coreos/etcd) as secondary.

```sh
ETCD_VER=v3.7.3

rm -rf /tmp/etcd-data.tmp && mkdir -p /tmp/etcd-data.tmp && \
  docker rmi gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:${ETCD_VER} || true && \
  docker run \
  -p 2379:2379 \
  -p 2380:2380 \
  --mount type=bind,source=/tmp/etcd-data.tmp,destination=/etcd-data \
  --name etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} \
  gcr.io/etcd-development/etcd:${ETCD_VER} \
  /usr/local/bin/etcd \
  --name s1 \
  --data-dir /etcd-data \
  --listen-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 \
  --advertise-client-urls http://0.0.0.0:2379 \
  --listen-peer-urls http://0.0.0.0:2380 \
  --initial-advertise-peer-urls http://0.0.0.0:2380 \
  --initial-cluster s1=http://0.0.0.0:2380 \
  --initial-cluster-token tkn \
  --initial-cluster-state new \
  --log-level info \
  --logger zap \
  --log-outputs stderr

docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcd --version
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl version
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdutl version
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl endpoint health
docker exec etcd-gcr-${ETCD_VER} /usr/local/bin/etcdctl put foo bar
```

### October 22, 2026

SECURITY:

* containers/alpine: Upgrade ca-certificates-bundle to 20261020-r0 to distrust eMudhra intermediate chains.
* containers/UBI: explicitly disallow emSign Root CA and Comodo AAA Services in the CA trust store to distrust eMudhra intermediate chains.
* core/policy: Fixed a cache-key collision vulnerability that could cause policy-name aliases to resolve to the immutable root policy. Root-policy aliases are now explicitly rejected at entity, group, token, authentication-response, and agent-registry policy assignment boundaries. Previously accepted root-equivalent policy aliases (e.g., "./root", "a/../root") are now rejected.

CHANGES:

* core: Bump Go version to 1.27.3 to resolve CVE-2026-111943.

IMPROVEMENTS:

* agent: Add auto auth SPIFFE method.

BUG FIXES:

* core/quotas (enterprise): Fixed a bug where role-based quotas would fail to determine roles where the role is stored as `form-data`.
* identity (enterprise): Fix updates to tpmgroup membership not taking effect on active node when the tpmgroup by-name endpoint is used for the update. Reads showed the change applied to storage, but the inmem index wasn't updated.
* identity/scim (enterprise): Fix `POST /Users` returning 409 instead of adopting an unmanaged entity whose name matches the `userName`, such as after `unlink-entity`. Adoption now depends only on the matching alias, and the name conflict check applies only when a new entity is created.
* managed-keys (enterprise): Fix wrapper error in using managed keys for MACs
* secrets/database/mssql: Safely quote database and user identifiers during default user revocation and parameterize principal lookups, so that logins whose names contain characters outside the database code page are removed rather than left disabled. Default password rotation now quotes the username and escapes the password.
storage/mssql, storage/mysql: Escape configured SQL identifiers when constructing storage queries.
* transit (enterprise): Fix key check to allow use of managed keys for HMAC
* transit (enterprise): Fix error with using CMAC keys after rotation from an HMAC key using the Rotate with Algorithm Change endpoint
* transit (enterprise): Fix error with using managed keys for datakey generation after rotation using the Rotate with Algorithm Change endpoint
* ui: Fix MFA form breadcrumbs rendering in enforcement section, updated radio cards to use HDS

## What's Changed

### Fixed
- Make the outbound credential headers mutually exclusive so a client-supplied credential can no longer override the gateway-injected upstream key: once BFE takes ownership of the upstream credential, the outbound request keeps only the header the request's `model_protocol` adapter injects and drops `Authorization` / `x-api-key` / `x-goog-api-key`, which used to be forwarded as-is — an upstream that prefers a residual header (kimi: `x-api-key` wins over `Authorization`; bailian: `Authorization` wins and never falls back) authenticated with the client token, answered 401, and that 401 was charged to the selected key: two requests from one client marked both kimi keys dead for 3600s, the cluster circuit-broke and traffic was silently degraded to `bailian/deepseek-v4.1-flash` while the client still saw 200 (issue #1447)

# Quick Start

data.name: Release 2.45.3 LTS
data.body:
## Known issues

- On Async Edge environments, an invalid update schedule date can be displayed when browsing a snapshot

### Known issues with Podman support

- Podman environments aren't supported by auto-onboarding script
- It's not possible to add Podman environments via socket, when running a Portainer server on Docker (and vice versa)
- Support for only CentOS 9, Podman 5 rootful

## Changes

### Breaking changes

- Portainer no longer trusts TLS certificates issued by eMudhra (emSign), following the compromise of eight eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943). Connections to services that present an affected certificate, including OAuth/OIDC and LDAPS providers, registries and Git hosts, will fail after the upgrade. If your single sign-on or LDAP provider is affected, only the initial admin will be able to sign in. Check your services before upgrading. [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)

### Security improvements

- Rejected Compose and Swarm stacks using `volumes_from` when non-administrators create, update, start or redeploy them with `Hide bind mounts for non-administrators` enabled, which let them inherit another container's host bind mounts
- Updated the Go toolchain to 1.26.10, fixing CVE-2026-56857 and CVE-2026-78663 (both Critical), along with CVE-2026-111943, CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-97031, CVE-2026-94440, CVE-2026-94439, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78667, CVE-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-56866, CVE-2026-94448 and CVE-2026-97030
- Removed the eMudhra emSign root certificates from the CA bundle in Linux images, and rejected certificate chains that contain the compromised eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943). [See this FAQ for details.](https://hubs.li/Q04B-qY30)
- Updated [golang.org/x/net](http://golang.org/x/net) to 0.60.0, fixing CVE-2026-78663 (Critical), CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-78669, CVE-2026-78660 and CVE-2026-78659 (all High)
- Updated helm in the kubectl shell image to v4.3.1, taking its Go toolchain to 1.27.2 and oras.land/oras-go/v2 to 2.6.2, fixing CVE-2026-39821 (Critical) and CVE-2026-50163 (High)
- Restricted kubeconfig tokens to the /api/endpoints/{id}/kubernetes proxy, so they are rejected with a 403 on every other API route, including admin-only routes and the Docker proxy. Kubeconfigs downloaded after upgrading carry a separate token per environment, limited to that environment 

### Bug fixes

- Fixed starting a container with an empty request body failing with a 400 error on Docker standalone and Swarm agent environments 
- Fixed GitOps sources starting a new poll while the previous one was still running, which could pile up overlapping redeploys on slow repositories. A poll that is still running now causes the next scheduled poll to be skipped
- Fixed GitOps workflows showing the Git reference and file path status as unknown after a stack was manually redeployed from Git. A manual redeploy now records these statuses for the stack's workflow artifact
- Fixed the YAML tab on the Kubernetes node details page going blank after switching tabs or refocusing the browser, and restored the missing gap between the tab content and the Applications table
- Fixed DockerHub pull rate limits and agent version detection failing on Docker engines newer than API 1.47, and, in BE, non-admin users with environment access getting 403 errors on `/agent/docker` and `/agent/host` routes, which left Swarm node selectors empty
- Fixed the search box on the Authentication logs page not filtering events by username

## Deprecated and removed features

None.

data.name: pack v0.40.10
data.body:
## Prerequisites

- A container runtime such as [Docker](https://www.docker.com/get-started) or [podman](https://podman.io/get-started) must be available to execute builds.

## Install

For instructions on installing `pack`, see our [installation docs](https://buildpacks.io/docs/tools/pack/cli/install/).

## Run

Run the command `pack`.

You should see the following output

```text
CLI for building apps using Cloud Native Buildpacks

Usage:
  pack [command]

Available Commands:
  build                 Generate app image from source code
  builder               Interact with builders
  buildpack             Interact with buildpacks
  extension             Interact with extensions
  config                Interact with your local pack config file
  inspect               Show information about a built app image
  stack                 (deprecated) Interact with stacks
  rebase                Rebase app image with latest run image
  sbom                  Interact with SBoM
  completion            Outputs completion script location
  report                Display useful information for reporting an issue
  version               Show current 'pack' version
  help                  Help about any command

Flags:
      --force-color   Force color output
  -h, --help          Help for 'pack'
      --no-color      Disable color output
  -q, --quiet         Show less output
      --timestamps    Enable timestamps in output
  -v, --verbose       Show more output
      --version       Show current 'pack' version

Use "pack [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```

## Info

Builders created with this release of the pack CLI contain [lifecycle v0.21.0](https://github.com/buildpack/lifecycle/releases/tag/v0.21.0) by default.

## Changelog

**This is a security-only patch release.** No feature work, no API change, no
intended behaviour change. If you are on v0.40.9, this is a drop-in upgrade.

### Security

Measured with the same scanner and vulnerability database, no suppressions applied:

| Image | Findings | Critical | High | Medium | **With a fix available** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `buildpacksio/pack:0.40.9` | 25 | 1 | 16 | 7 | **21** |
| `buildpacksio/pack:0.40.10` | **5** | 0 | 1 | 3 | **1** |
| default lifecycle, before (`0.21.0`) | 61 | 4 | 36 | 18 | **53** |
| default lifecycle, after (`0.21.25`) | **5** | 2 | 1 | 1 | **0** |

#### Toolchain

* Bump Go to 1.26.9 and security-relevant dependencies (#2713)
* Bump Go to 1.26.10 for CVE-2026-111943 (#2720)

#### Dependencies

| Module | Bump | Advisory | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `golang.org/x/crypto` | v0.54.0 → v0.57.0 | `CVE-2026-78662`, `CVE-2026-56855` — DoS on deadlocked `ssh` channels | — |
| `golang.org/x/net` *(indirect)* | v0.56.0 → v0.60.0 | `CVE-2026-78659/78660/78663/78669/97032` — HTTP/2 memory exhaustion, malformed framing headers, double flow-control refund, HPACK encoder race | — |
| `github.com/moby/go-archive` | v0.2.0 → v0.3.3 | `GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h` / `CVE-2026-17106` — crafted tar can write outside the extraction directory | **High** |
| `github.com/moby/sys/user` | v0.4.0 → v0.4.1 | `GHSA-mjcv-p78q-w5fw` / `CVE-2026-61801` — DoS via unbounded parsing of user/group files | Moderate |


#### Still outstanding, and why

| Advisory | Why it remains |
| --- | --- |
| `GHSA-7236-3392-c5c6` (buildkit, Medium) | **The one finding with an available fix.** It describes a custom BuildKit *frontend* disabling Seccomp/AppArmor during a solve. `pack` never runs a solve — it links only `frontend/dockerfile/{command,instructions,linter,parser,shell}` and `util/{stack,suggest}`; `solver`, `executor`, `frontend/gateway`, `client` and `session` are absent. The fix needs buildkit v0.31.1 → go-containerregistry v0.21.6 → an imgutil bump, so it is held for 0.41.0. |
| `GO-2026-4883`, `GO-2026-4887` (docker/docker) | Daemon-side code paths. `pack` only ever uses Docker as a client. Fixed only in `moby/moby` v2. |
| `GHSA-685w-q87j-wqw3` (docker/distribution, Medium) | Missing digest verification in `registry/client.(*manifests).Get`. No `ManifestService` is ever constructed — the only importer of that package in the whole linked set uses three HTTP error helpers. No fix exists for the v2 module. |
| `GO-2026-6225` (`docker-credential-acr-env`) | Unmaintained upstream, no fixed version. Severity Unknown. Left **visible** in scan output rather than suppressed. |


### Bugs

* Pass the format string directly to `Debugf` (#2712)

### Maintenance

* Propagate the Go 1.26 bump to the hard-coded Go pins (#2715)
* Fix the duplicate-issue search in the release canary (#2716)
* Assert the annotation we set, not the total annotation count (#2717)
* Don't assert temp-dir cleanup on Windows in the registry buildpack test (#2722)

### Breaking changes

None.

### Upgrade notes

* Contributors need Go **1.26.10+** locally. `make verify` builds `golangci-lint`  with the *system* Go, so a system Go whose language version trails `go.mod` fails lint even though CI passes.
* Builders rebuilt with this release pick up lifecycle **0.21.25**. Existing builders are unaffected until rebuilt.

## Contributors

We'd like to acknowledge that this release wouldn't be as good without the help of the following amazing contributors:

@jjbustamante

data.body:
## 1.17.0 (October 21, 2026)


NEW FEATURES:

* Terraform now supports variables and locals in provider requirements ([#39153](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/39153))

* A new `-minimal-refresh` planning option has been added, which will only refresh resources that have proposed changes. ([#35290](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/35290))

* policy: Terraform Policy is now generally available. The `-policies` flag for `plan`, `apply`, and `query` no longer requires an experimental build or the `-allow-experimental-features` flag. Query policies evaluate resources discovered by list blocks and report human-readable or JSON results. See https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/policy for more information. ([#38970](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38970))


ENHANCEMENTS:

* command/init: Enrich log messages with provider versions ([#38918](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38918))

* test: Add mock_provider support for ephemeral resources ([#38928](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38928))

* command/login: display warning after successful login if user is subject to an organization's TTL policy


BUG FIXES:

* funcs: pow and log no longer panic when result is not a number ([#38912](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38912))

* ephemeral: Terraform will now use and display diagnostics raised when _renewing_ an ephemeral resource. This may cause warnings to appear that previously were lost. We expect that any error diagnostics that were previously lost would have caused confusing downstream errors, so we do not anticipate this change to be breaking. ([#38989](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38989))

* test: Deterministic dependency ordering in cleanup graph ([#38247](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38247))

* query: report Unknown and N/A results for policy evaluations of discovered resources ([#39058](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/39058))

* query: `terraform query -policies` now rejects a path that is not a directory, instead of passing it on to the policy engine ([#39238](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/39238))

* funcs: The `log` and `pow` functions now raise errors when they return +/- Infinity, as this result is not usable in downstream code. ([#39304](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/39304))

* show: Read variable values from the plan file when showing a local plan ([#39362](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/39362))


NOTES:

* version: JSON output now includes a new `format_version` field, which will enable safer future changes of the command's JSON output format. It is assumed existing tooling ignores unknown fields and therefore this change should not be breaking in itself but we advice consumers to pay attention to `format_version` in future releases and/or use latest version of hashicorp/terraform-json & hashicorp/terraform-exec which does. ([#38930](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/38930))

* Terraform is now built with Go 1.26.10, which no longer trusts certificates issued through a set of compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs (CVE-2026-111943) ([#39417](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/39417))

data.body:
# v2.8.6 Release Notes

This patch release fixes PhysicalMachineChaos validation and UID handling, Dashboard behavior, and IOChaos file creation on newer Linux kernels.

> [!NOTE]
> In this release, we have extensively utilized AI to enhance our efficiency in making improvements. Of course, manual review is also indispensable. With the help of partial manual corrections, we find that AI is greatly boosting our productivity, which will significantly alleviate the manpower shortage problem in our maintainer team. If you encounter any issues, please feel free to let us know by submitting an issue. Thanks for using Chaos Mesh! 😃

### Changed

- Upgrade toda to v0.2.5 to fix IOChaos temporary file creation on newer Linux kernels [#5128](https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/pull/5128)

### Fixed

- Reject PhysicalMachineChaos injection when `spec.uid` is empty and point users to the mutating webhook configuration [#5148](https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/pull/5148)
- Preserve `spec.uid` when importing PhysicalMachineChaos YAML into the Dashboard and submitting the form [#5149](https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/pull/5149)
- Allow PhysicalMachineChaos HTTP actions in standalone experiments, schedules, and workflows [#5142](https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/pull/5142)
- Accept valid Redis expiration options and percentage-only cache limits in PhysicalMachineChaos [#5141](https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/pull/5141)
- Prevent Total Experiments Status chart from shrinking on dashboard navigation [#5077](https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/pull/5077)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/chaos-mesh/chaos-mesh/compare/v2.8.5...v2.8.6

- [SECURITY] Container images: Update CA certificates to distrust "emSign ECC Root CA - G3" and "Comodo AAA Services root" following the compromise of eMudhra intermediate CA private keys.
- [SECURITY] Build with Go 1.27.3 to fix vulnerabilities in `net/http`, `net/textproto`, `crypto/tls` and `html/template`.
- [SECURITY] Bump golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 to fix HTTP/2 vulnerabilities (GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6612, GO-2026-6617).
.......... [ZBXNEXT-826] updated release date for 8.0.0rc2

data.name: v2.1.0
data.body:
## 2.1.0 (October 21, 2026)
BREAKING CHANGES:

* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Agent HTTP API request bodies are now limited to 512 KiB by default, including chunked requests and requests with an unsupported method, and oversized requests return HTTP 413 before the body is read in full. Very large `/v1/config` writes that previously succeeded can now fail. Raise the limit with the new `limits.http_max_request_body_size` setting if needed.
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Resource API (`/api/...`) request bodies are now subject to the same `limits.http_max_request_body_size` limit (512 KiB by default), and oversized requests return HTTP 413.
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** `GET /v1/agent/connect/ca/leaf/:service` now requires `service:write` on the requested service for every request, including requests served from the agent's cached leaf certificate. Requests with no token or a token without that permission now receive HTTP 403 instead of the cached certificate. Callers must present a token with `service:write` for the service.
* catalog: **(Enterprise only)** `Catalog.Register` now requires write permission on the node or service of an existing health check when updating it. Tokens that previously updated checks without that permission now receive a permission denied error.
* cli: Migrated the `consul connect redirect-traffic` command from `iptables`/`ip6tables` to `nftables` (`nft`). The command now uses the `sdk/nftables` package, which applies all IPv4 and IPv6 rules atomically in a single pass via the `nftables` `inet` address family, instead of separate `iptables` and `ip6tables` invocations. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* cli: Transparent proxy exclusions are now validated before rules are applied: user IDs must be numeric and outbound exclusions must be IP addresses or CIDRs. `iptables` previously also accepted user names, UID ranges, and host names. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* cli: `consul connect redirect-traffic` does not remove `iptables`/`ip6tables` rules created by earlier Consul versions. This only matters when upgrading an existing host or VM in place. Before running the new command on an existing host or VM, remove any Consul-managed `iptables` rules first (see the transparent proxy upgrade guide for a reference cleanup script). Leaving both rule sets in place can cause double NAT or inconsistent traffic redirection. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* docker: The official Consul container images now include `nftables` instead of `iptables`. Scripts that run `iptables` inside the Consul image must be updated. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* sdk: Replaced the `iptables` package with a new `nftables` package for transparent proxy traffic redirection. Traffic redirection now requires the `nft` binary and a Linux kernel with stateful NAT support in `nftables` `inet` family chains, available upstream starting with Linux kernel version 5.2 (some distributions backport this support onto an earlier nominal kernel version, for example RHEL 8+, kernel 4.18+, and its derivatives). There is no automatic fallback to `iptables`/`ip6tables`, so hosts without this kernel support will fail to set up transparent proxy redirection. [[GH-23785](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23785)]
* feature-gates: Gate API Gateway HTTPRoute upstream-routing composition (PR #23294) behind the experimental feature `api-gateway-upstream-routing`. When disabled (default), the legacy HTTPRoute-to-router shape is preserved exactly. When enabled by an operator after a full datacenter upgrade, service-router rules are composed with HTTPRoute matches, resolver subset definitions are preserved, and discovery-chain watches use the correct HTTP protocol override. Existing agentless API Gateway proxy states are rebuilt automatically when the effective gate value changes.

SECURITY:

* Upgrade go version to 1.26.10 to address security vulnerabilities. [[GH-24067](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24067)]
* deps: upgrade `github.com/hashicorp/go-discover` to v1.5.0, removing the dependency on the archived `github.com/hashicorp/vic` module. This also upgrades `github.com/vmware/govmomi` to v0.55.1 and adds an `srv` provider for cloud auto-join. [[GH-24021](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24021)]
* security: **(Enterprise only)** Remove the `github.com/hashicorp/consul` root module dependency from the `test-integ` fault-injection tests to address [CVE-2026-15972](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15972) and [CVE-2026-88021](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-88021).
* security: Remove the `github.com/hashicorp/consul` root module dependency from the envoy integration test SDS server, the `consul-container` and `test-integ` test modules, and the `proto-gen-rpc-glue` e2e fixture to address [CVE-2026-15972](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-15972). [[GH-24043](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24043)]
* deps: Upgrade github.com/hashicorp/raft-wal to v0.5.0 (with raft v1.8.0, serf v0.11.0, memberlist v0.7.0 and go-metrics v0.7.0), removing the dependency on github.com/coreos/etcd. [[GH-23985](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23985)]
* deps: Upgrade golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 to address GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6603, GO-2026-6617 and GO-2026-6612. [[GH-23994](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23994)]
* docker: Run `apk upgrade` when building the Alpine-based container images so base-image packages (such as sqlite and jq) are up to date. [[GH-23964](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23964)]
* oauth: **(Enterprise only)** Avoid an unchecked size addition when merging JWKS key sets during OAuth key rotation.
* security: Upgrade github.com/klauspost/compress to v1.18.7, go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver to v1.17.10, github.com/moby/go-archive to v0.3.0 and github.com/go-openapi/swag to v0.27.1 to address CVE-2026-63209, CVE-2026-88031, CVE-2026-2303, CVE-2026-17106 and CVE-2026-85280. [[GH-23964](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23964)]
* ui: Add Content-Security-Policy header to Consul UI HTTP responses to mitigate XSS and data injection attacks. [[GH-23971](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23971)]
* ui: Pin a newer resolution of morgan to 1.12.1 to address GHSA-9f6g-j8ch-79g4 [[GH-23952](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23952)]
* Added debounce behavior to enforce a minimum interval between expensive federation-state anti-entropy sync operations. [[GH-23196](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23196)]
* Update `brace-expansion` to address [GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rgw5-rvv9-x895) (DoS via unbounded intermediate arrays). [[GH-23786](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23786)]
* Update `fast-uri` to address [GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7p8r-x3mc-p8w7) (Host Confusion via backslash authority introducer). [[GH-23786](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23786)]
* Update `socket.io-parser` to address [CVE-2026-69185](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2m8v-j782-fhvr) (Zero-attachment Memory Exhaustion). [[GH-23786](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23786)]

FEATURES:

* acl: Add OIDC RP-Initiated IdP logout for tokens created via an `oidc` auth method: `consul logout` prints the identity provider's logout URL for the user to open (or opens it in the default browser with the new `-open-browser` flag or `CONSUL_LOGOUT_OPEN_BROWSER` environment variable), and the web UI opens it on logout, terminating the IdP session. Activates automatically when the IdP advertises an `end_session_endpoint` in its OIDC discovery document, or when the logout endpoint is configured explicitly with the new `OIDCLogoutURL` auth method setting for providers that do not advertise one. [[GH-23739](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23739)]
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Add an inline `ai` block to service definitions, letting a workload declare its AI role (`inference-model`, `mcp-server`, or `ai-agent`) and role-specific configuration in a single registration via config files and HTTP APIs. [[GH-13032](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13032)]
* api-gateway: Add `http2` and `grpc` as valid API Gateway listener protocols, enabling end-to-end HTTP/2 and gRPC from client to backend. Previously only `http` and `tcp` were accepted; the gateway would silently downgrade gRPC/HTTP2 traffic to HTTP/1.1 on the upstream hop. The new protocols render the correct downstream HTTP connection manager (HTTP/2 codec, `h2,http/1.1` ALPN) and align the upstream cluster to HTTP/2, closing the parity gap with Ingress Gateway. [[GH-23784](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23784)]
* api-gateway: Auto-register DNS for services exposed via an API Gateway, resolvable at `<service>.api-gateway.consul`. Populates the `gateway-services` catalog mapping for API Gateways and adds DNS SANs to the API Gateway Connect leaf certificate, bringing API Gateway to parity with Ingress Gateway. The feature is version-gated and backfills pre-existing gateways automatically once all servers are upgraded. [[GH-23647](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23647)]
* api-gateway: Support zero-touch downstream TLS termination. When `TLS { Enabled = true }` is set on an `api-gateway` config entry with no inline/file-system/SDS certificate, the gateway terminates downstream TLS using its Connect CA leaf certificate (with `*.api-gateway.consul` DNS SANs). Explicitly configured certificates continue to take precedence and are served as SNI overrides alongside the leaf default chain. [[GH-23647](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23647)]
* api-gateway: add `PassiveHealthCheck` to gateway-level default upstream limits and route service-level limit overrides, so passive health checking (Envoy outlier detection) can be configured for services routed through an API gateway. [[GH-23783](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23783)]
* cli: **(Enterprise only)** `consul connect envoy -gateway=inference` launches the policy processor alongside Envoy and enforces a minimum Envoy version for the inference gateway. The ext_proc socket is derived per proxy instance; `-ext-proc-socket-dir` overrides its directory (default `/var/run/consul`).
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Added an agent-managed OAuth client lifecycle for services with `ai.role` of `ai-agent` or `mcp-server`, including dynamic client registration with IBM Security Verify, key rotation, JWKS publication, and SDS delivery of the OAuth client credential to `ai-agent` Envoy sidecars.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Deliver OAuth sidecar credentials as AES-256-GCM envelopes. Content-encryption keys are persisted in KV and served via WorkloadKeyService.FetchKey so consul-obo-outbound can decrypt without becoming an SDS client.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Wire consul-obo-outbound and consul-obo-inbound ext_proc filters into connect-proxy xDS for hop-bound on-behalf-of token exchange.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Register services with `ai.role` of `ai-agent` or `mcp-server` with IBM Security Verify using `private_key_jwt`, persist DCR/JWKS in KV, and deliver the client credential to Envoy as SDS GenericSecret JSON for `ai-agent` workloads. Cluster IAM is an OIDC ACL auth method with `EnableServiceDCR=true` (agent `oauth.iam` HCL is rejected).
* connect: add `ecdh_curves` to `mesh` config entries (`MeshDirectionalTLSConfig`) and `tls_ecdh_curves` to agent TLS configuration (`TLSProtocolConfig`) to support configuring allowed ECDH/KEM curves for sidecar mTLS and agent RPC/HTTPS/gRPC, with automatic hybrid Post-Quantum `X25519MLKEM768` curve injection when `tls_min_version` is set to `TLSv1_3`. [[GH-23884](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23884)]
* feature-gates: Add Raft-backed dynamic feature gate framework (Phase 1). A new `feature_gates { bootstrap = { ... } }` server configuration block seeds the first Raft policy. The leader continuously reconciles desired policy, minimum-version eligibility, and registry defaults into a committed resolved status. Every server runs an atomic cache populated only from committed FSM state; agents consume an indexed resolved snapshot and fail closed until the first generation is delivered. New operator CLI commands `consul operator feature list`, `get`, and `set` provide CAS-safe, ACL-protected inspection and control of feature gates.
* operator: Add `GET /v1/operator/features`, `GET /v1/operator/feature/:name`, and `PUT /v1/operator/feature/:name` HTTP endpoints for reading and updating feature gate state. Reads require `operator:read`; writes require `operator:write`. All reads are blocking-query capable. [[GH-23791](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23791)]
* inference-gateway: **(Enterprise only)** Route opted-in external inference models through a terminating gateway. Models marked with the terminating-gateway egress are discovered from the catalog, resolved through the mesh discovery chain, and load-balanced across healthy terminating-gateway replicas, with capability-pool priority tiers and fail-closed behavior when no valid transport is available. A capability pool containing an external model is rejected, and its capability route returns 503, when two of its models render the same endpoint address or its model weights cannot be represented exactly.
* inference-gateway: **(Enterprise only)** Add the `inference-gateway` service kind and config entry. The gateway terminates inbound mesh mTLS, enforces intentions, and applies PII and routing policy through an ext_proc filter to a co-located policy processor. Model upstreams are services registered with `ai.role = "inference-model"` that intentions allow and that are reachable through the mesh (connect-enabled or behind a terminating gateway). The gateway connects to them over mTLS and selects them by capability, failing over across providers by priority.
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added server-side product usage metrics for ACL auth method counts (OIDC, Kubernetes, JWT) and audit logging config.
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added server-side product usage metrics for mesh gateway mode counts: `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_remote.count` and `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_local.count` report the number of service instances configured to use each mesh gateway mode, and `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_none.count` reports the number of service instances with no explicit mesh gateway mode (unset or `none`).
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added server-side product usage metrics for service intention default policy, service intention L7 and JWT counts
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added the server-side product usage metric `consul.usage.mesh_gateway_enabled`, which reports whether any mesh gateway instance is registered in the cluster. It is independent of the mesh gateway mode counts: those count connect-proxy sidecars by their upstream routing mode, while this reports whether the gateway capability is deployed at all.
* terminating-gateway: **(Enterprise only)** Add Vault-backed credential injection at the terminating gateway egress. A `TerminatingGateway` config entry now carries a `CredentialInjection` block (ext_proc processor UDS path and message timeout) and each linked service can declare a `Credential` binding (`Mode: "inject"` with a `BindingID`). At egress, an ext_proc filter calls a co-located processor that injects the bound credential (e.g. a provider API key sourced from Vault) into the upstream request, so credentials are never stored in mesh config or exposed to clients.
* xds: Add an inline "virtual DNS" UDP listener (127.0.0.1:8653) that serves an in-memory FQDN-to-VIP table derived from the proxy snapshot. It advertises VIPs for explicit upstreams, intention-allowed upstreams in transparent proxy mode, and cluster peering upstreams, while skipping cross-partition VIPs, stale/unauthorized discovery chains, and empty or non-IP entries so DNS responses stay in sync with what the transparent-proxy listener will actually intercept. Add an optional "egress DNS" UDP listener (127.0.0.1:8654) that forwards queries to agent-configured DNS recursors via c-ares when recursors are present. Extend the xDS `ConfigFetcher` interface (and agent implementation) to expose DNS recursors. [[GH-23698](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23698)]

IMPROVEMENTS:

* chore: Update of actions/cache/restore from 4.2.0 to 6.1.0
* chore: Update of actions/download-artifact from 4.1.7 to 8.0.2 [[GH-13634](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13634)]
* chore: Update of actions/upload-artifact from 4.3.3 to 7.0.2 [[GH-13635](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13635)]
* chore: Update of hashicorp/vault-action from 3 to 4 [[GH-13636](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13636)]
* connect: **(Enterprise Only)** update compatibility tests to Nomad ENT v1.9.13+ent, v1.10.17+ent, v1.11.11+ent, v2.0.7+ent and Vault ENT 1.19.22+ent, 1.20.16+ent, 1.21.11+ent, 2.0.4+ent, 2.1.1+ent and envoy 1.39.4, 1.38.7, 1.37.9, 1.36.13
* connect: revert the maximum supported Envoy version from 1.39.4 back to 1.39.1. Envoy 1.39.4 support, listed in a prior release note, is not included in this release. [[GH-24057](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24057)]
* connect: deliver the sidecar proxy's leaf certificate and CA roots to Envoy over SDS instead of embedding them inline in the public listener. Leaf certificate rotation is now a hitless hot-swap that no longer changes the listener filter chain hash, so established connections (notably long-lived TCP sessions) are no longer drained and terminated on every rotation. [[GH-23938](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23938)]
* terminating-gateway: deliver each linked service's Connect leaf certificate and the shared CA roots to Envoy over SDS instead of embedding them inline in the gateway's downstream filter chains. Leaf rotation no longer changes the filter chain hash, so established connections through the gateway are no longer drained. [[GH-23938](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23938)]
* api-gateway: add `invert` field to `HTTPHeaderMatch` in `http-route` config entries, enabling negated header match conditions (e.g. "route when header is absent" or "route when header value does NOT match"). Brings API Gateway to parity with the Ingress Gateway's existing `Invert` support in `service-router`. [[GH-23817](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23817)]
* ci: **(Enterprise only)** Increased the stale PR automation windows to 90 days before marking a pull request stale and 60 days before closing it. [[GH-13119](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13119)]
* peering: **(Enterprise only)** Add support for routing traffic to named ports on peered multiport services. [[GH-13142](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/13142)]
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added three product usage metrics for auto-encrypt visibility. `consul.usage.client_agent_metric_included` reports whether client-agent metrics collection is enabled. `consul.usage.client_auto_encrypt_enabled.count` and `consul.usage.server_auto_encrypt_enabled.count` reports the number of clients and servers, respectively, with `auto_encrypt.tls` enabled. `consul.usage.auto_encrypt_enabled` combines both counts into a single boolean — true if auto-encrypt is enabled anywhere in the cluster be it client or server.
* telemetry: **(Enterprise only)** Added three server-side product usage metrics, `consul.usage.api_gateway.enabled` reports whether any API gateway instances are currently registered in the cluster, `consul.usage.mesh.service.percentage` reports the percentage of service instances that are connect-proxy sidecars and `consul.usage.transparent_proxy.enabled.percentage` reports the percentage of connect-proxy instances that have transparent proxy mode enabled.
* ui: Migrate the Consul UI to the HashiCorp Design System (HDS). This covers the global navigation shell and breadcrumbs, the list pages (key/value, peers, auth methods, services, service instances, nodes, intentions, linked services, upstreams, and access control), and the access control, namespace, and admin partition forms. Includes numerous accessibility (A11y) fixes. [[GH-23911](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23911)]
* xds: **(Enterprise only)** External inference-model upstreams are rendered with a destination-specific mTLS transport socket (per-model SDS validation context and SNI/SAN matching), so the gateway-to-model hop for terminating-gateway-fronted models is mutually authenticated and encrypted per model.
* xds: **(Enterprise only)** The `builtin/ext-proc` Envoy extension now supports Unix domain socket processor targets via `Target.Path`.

BUG FIXES:

* gateway: Fix a data race in the API gateway controller where the route reconciler kept adding to a `WatchSet` after handing it to a controller trigger that was already iterating it. The trigger is now registered only after all discovery chain reads are complete. [[GH-24018](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24018)]
* ui: Render tab content inside its tab panel so assistive technology can associate it with its tab, and keep focus on a tab after activating it [[GH-24013](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24013)]
* ui: Show errors loading a tab's content inside the page instead of as a second nested page [[GH-24013](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/24013)]
* acl: **(Enterprise only)** Fixed Envoy escape-hatch key matching in `Proxy.Config` and per-upstream config so it follows the same case-folding rules as the config decoders. Keys that differ only by Unicode case folding (for example `envoy_local_cluſter_json`), and Go field-name forms such as `EnvoyListenerJSON`, now require `mesh:write` like their canonical spellings.
* agent: (Enterprise only) Fixed audit logging so request-body capture respects the body-size limit, uses the decoded request path when excluding KV bodies (for example `/v1/k%76/...`), and skips `/v1/txn` bodies. `POST /v1/operator/audit-hash` now returns HTTP 413 for oversized bodies.
* agent: **(Enterprise only)** Fixed `PUT /v1/kv/` so chunked request bodies are bounded by `kv_max_value_size`, matching the existing `Content-Length` check.
* proxycfg: Fixed a goroutine and memory leak where a proxy's watches kept running after its state stopped unexpectedly, because replacing, deregistering or closing a stopped state did not cancel them. [[GH-23990](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23990)]
* proxycfg: Fixed a goroutine and memory leak where transparent proxies registered a new health watch for every imported peered service each time the imported services list changed, and never stopped watches for removed upstreams. [[GH-23990](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23990)]
* telemetry: Restore Raft, Serf, and Memberlist metrics in release artifacts by building with the `hashicorpmetrics` tag. [[GH-23813](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23813)]
* agent/xds: Fixed an issue where cross-cluster and peered requests originating from an API Gateway were rejected with HTTP 403 Forbidden by downstream service RBAC intentions. Trailing semicolon-separated fields in the client certificate component of the `x-forwarded-client-cert` (XFCC) header (such as auto-registered DNS SANs) are now properly accepted by the RBAC principal regular expression. [[GH-23920](https://github.com/hashicorp/consul/issues/23920)]
* cli: **(Enterprise only)** `consul intention create` now creates and replaces intentions via the exact (config-entry) intention API used by the UI, which supports non-default admin partitions (for example `-partition team-a`). Per-source metadata (`-meta`) continues to use the deprecated legacy intention API and is only supported in the default partition; combining `-meta` with a non-default partition now fails with a clear, actionable error. To attach metadata to intentions in an admin partition, use a `service-intentions` config entry with entry-level `Meta` via `consul config write`.
* connect: **(Enterprise only)** Attach outbound OBO only for identity-plane upstreams (`ai-agent` / `mcp-server`). Explicit HTTP upstreams to inference-gateway or inference-model destinations no longer get consul-obo-outbound and fail closed with "OBO audience not configured".
* connect: Fixed a bug where Consul servers ignored the configured `default_intention_policy` for three server-side surfaces — the intention check API (`consul intention check`, `GET /v1/connect/intentions/check`), the service topology view (`Internal.ServiceTopology`), and transparent proxy upstream discovery (`Internal.IntentionUpstreams`) — and fell back to `acl.default_policy` instead. This only changes behavior when `default_intention_policy` and `acl.default_policy` are set to opposite values; when they agree (or `default_intention_policy` is unset) there is no change. With `default_intention_policy=deny` and `acl.default_policy=allow`, the check API and topology previously reported connections as allowed even though they were denied; with `default_intention_policy=allow` and `acl.default_policy=deny`, transparent proxy sidecars under-provisioned their upstreams and could fail to reach services they were authorized to reach. Envoy RBAC enforcement was not affected and already honored `default_intention_policy`.

update to go1.26.10
These releases include 1 security fix following the security policy:

- crypto/x509: mitigation for security concerns with a specific Certificate Authority

  We're blocking trust in a small set of intermediate certificates due to specific security concerns around their operation.

  Verify will now filter out chains which contain these intermediates, preventing them from being returned to the caller.

  We highly recommend immediately upgrading to this release.

  This is CVE-2026-111943 and Go issue https://go.dev/issue/82345.

This release improves DNS caching, forwarding, and transport reliability,
with fixes for stale-cache handling, upstream connections, crashes/race fixes,
as well as enhancemence from quite a few plugins.

Forwarding now supports DNS-over-QUIC upstreams. Additional new features include
optional JSON query logging, authenticated RFC 2136 dynamic DNS updates, SIIT support,
expr-lang templates, and PROXY protocol v2 metadata.

The release is built with Go 1.27.3, covering CVE-2026-56865, CVE-2026-56864,
CVE-2026-33818, CVE-2026-97032, CVE-2026-78659, CVE-2026-97031, and CVE-2026-111943, along with
other security fixes.

plugin/cache: Cache SERVFAIL when the resolver fails without a response (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8629)
plugin/cache: Clarify stale verify behavior (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8579)
plugin/cache: Don't cache or panic on responses with no question (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8467)

plugin/clouddns: Add endpoint directive (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8618)
plugin/clouddns: Add refresh directive (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8616)
plugin/dns64: Fixes a nil pointer dereference panic in dns64 during response (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8511)
plugin/dns64: Preserve A fallback response codes (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8619)

plugin/etcd: Stop target stripping at the end of a name (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8584)
plugin/file: Fix less is not up to RFC 1034 and 4034 (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8503)
plugin/file: Fix race condition in file plugin closer (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8583)
plugin/file: Reject SOA owners that do not match the zone (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8555)
plugin/file: Return SERVFAIL on self-referential CNAME loops (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8475)
plugin/file: Test that out-of-zone CNAME targets keep NOERROR (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8569)
plugin/file: Track zone mtime for reload_by_mtime (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8556)
plugin/forward: Bound DoT connection setup for retries (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8543)
plugin/forward: Ensure forward sets the DoH host (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8470)
plugin/forward: Set IP_RECVERR on upstream UDP sockets (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8628)
plugin/forward: Support DNS-over-QUIC upstreams (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8474)
plugin/forward: Treat forward upstream hostnames as absolute FQDNs to avoid search-domain resolution. (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8563)
plugin/grpc: Close clients on shutdown (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8582)
plugin/grpc_server: Both limits accept zero, not only positive integers (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8660)
plugin/hosts: Don't drop entries after an over-long line (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8496)
plugin/hosts: Don't drop over-long fields silently (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8551)
plugin/hosts: Parse hosts files with bufio.Reader (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8516)
plugin/https: Add max_streams to limit HTTP/2 concurrent streams (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8522)
plugin/k8s_external: Correct the SOA example in the docs (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8666)
plugin/k8s_external: Fixes a nil pointer dereference panic when upstream lookup returns no response (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8518)
plugin/kubernetes: Include structured key/value context in client-go logs (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8490)
plugin/kubernetes: Isolate NS address test fixtures (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8513)
plugin/kubernetes: Support pods with multiple IPs (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8635)
plugin/loadbalance: Reduce roundRobin allocations for homogeneous address sets (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8375)
plugin/loadbalance: Validate the response before dereferencing it in WriteMsg (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8523)
plugin/metrics: Drop the nonexistent type label from request_duration_seconds (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8650)
plugin/metrics: Release listener on TLS startup failure (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8527)
plugin/minimal: Fixes a nil pointer dereference panic in minimal prefetch response processing (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8506)
plugin/proxyproto: Expose PPv2 TLVs to downstream plugins as metadata (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8641)
plugin/proxyproto: Preserve the UDP peer for LOCAL (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8581)
plugin/quic: Add max_connections directive (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8610)
plugin/ready: Release lock before server shutdown (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8526)
plugin/reload: Broadcast shutdown signal (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8504)
plugin/rewrite: Drop the per-record dot-prefixed temporary in remapStringRewriter (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8382)
plugin/rewrite: Fixes a nil pointer dereference panic in ResponseReverter.WriteMsg (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8519)
plugin/rewrite: Limit rewrite cname recursion (https://github.com/coredns/coredns/pull/8570)

data.name: v5.1.1
data.body:
## Improvements

- Update background task records to omit original args and kwargs at creation, reducing unnecessary parameter persistence
- Strengthen persistent write protection for databases and Redis in high availability deployments across container restarts, recreation, and failure recovery
- Improve redeployment completion checks to tolerate normal replication lag, and refine switchover waits and recovery coordination to reduce false failure detection

## Bug Fixes

- Validate Access Token format while preserving fallback compatibility with other Bearer Token authentication methods
- Fix NLA configuration and RDP service refresh during Tinker applet host deployment, checking Group Policy and disabling listener NLA before installation, then verifying the configuration afterward; stop deployment with clear guidance when Group Policy requires NLA
- Fix race conditions involving role callbacks, operation locks, and file synchronization acknowledgments during switchover, automatic rejoin, and startup recovery [JumpServer EE]
- Improve MySQL/MariaDB replication position handling and crash recovery, and fix a race condition in PostgreSQL replication slot cleanup during standby rebuilds [JumpServer EE]
- Fix local administrator credential recovery and health checks during MySQL/MariaDB maintenance, avoiding the use of peer credentials or stale application passwords [JumpServer EE]

Bug#40126952: Fix openSUSE 16 server package account conflicts

Declare user and group virtual provides for mysql and mysqlrouter on
openSUSE 16. Each package already creates its corresponding account
before installing directories owned by that account.

This resolves RPM account dependency conflicts during installation.

## [28.2.0] - 2026-10-18
